chunks.text: Trial AEG-TR-001 evaluates an oral glucose-lowering agent in adults with type 2 diabetes. Participants with estimated glomerular filtration rate below 45 are excluded.
Metformin dosing for adults starts at 500 mg once daily with meals and titrates to a maximum of 2000 mg per day. Metformin is contraindicated when eGFR is below 30.
Warfarin combined with aspirin increases the risk of bleeding. Monitor INR closely and review antiplatelet therapy before co-prescribing.
NSAIDs such as ibuprofen can reduce renal function in patients with chronic kidney disease and may affect blood pressure control with ACE inhibitors.
First-line management of hypertension in adults includes thiazide-type diuretics, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or calcium channel blockers, selected by comorbidity.
Elevated high-sensitivity troponin with ischemic symptoms supports a diagnosis of myocardial infarction. Serial measurements are required.
Trial AEG-TR-002 is a phase II study of an anti-inflammatory biologic in moderate ulcerative colitis. The primary endpoint is clinical remission at week 12.
Simvastatin given with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as clarithromycin raises the risk of myopathy. Dose limits apply.
An HbA1c of 6.5 percent or higher on two occasions supports a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes.
Deep vein thrombosis presents with unilateral leg swelling and pain. Confirm with compression ultrasonography.
ACE inhibitors can cause hyperkalaemia and a dry cough. Check potassium and creatinine within two weeks of starting therapy.
Participants must give written informed consent before any trial-specific procedure is performed.

mandates.mandate: Avoid NSAIDs: chronic kidney disease stage 3.
Metformin dose must not exceed 2000 mg per day.
No warfarin co-prescription without INR review.
